newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks firm, further gains expected.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks firm, further gains expected.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mostly higher on Friday and traders predicted the upward trend would continue in the following days.
"Blue chips and other popular stocks are likely to keep going up in the next few days, lifted by a sudden wave of investment," Marko Nikolac of Metroholding brokerage told Reuters.
He said investors were probably moved to act by common expectations that Croatia would get good credit rating some time this month.
Of ten active issues on Friday six were up, two flat and two down.
Biggest gainer, chocolate maker Kras was up 37 kuna to 500, on volume of 957 units.
Fully-listed drugs firm Pliva, the most actively traded issue, edged up eight kuna to 405 on volume of 2,301 shares.
Nikolac said the recent share-split at 37 for one would probably be beneficial for the stock in the future.
The other blue chip Zagrebacka Banka gained ten kuna to close at 1,070, but sold only 70 shares.
Hoteliers Laguna and Jadranturist, adding 30 and 25 kuna to 1,060 and 250 kuna respectively were also among the gainers.
Volume was higher at 7,484 units and so was turnover at 2.5 million kuna.
Biggest decliner hotelier Arenaturist lost 8 kuna from over a month ago to close at 142, selling 96 shares.
